messages.content: I need all pending and active mandates of users parath and bhanu

function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.reasoning:
The user wants all pending and active mandates of users named Parath and Bhanu. We have two functions: user_mandates(name, status?) and partner_mandates(status?). They want mandates for specific users. So we should call user_mandates twice? Or maybe we can combine? The function signature only allows one name at a time. So we need to call it twice: once for Parath, once for Bhanu. But they also want both pending and active mandates. The function accepts status optional; default active. We could call with status=active then status=pending. That would be four calls. But maybe we can just call with status unspecified (default active) and then filter manually? But we can't get pending ones without specifying status. So we need separate calls.

We might ask clarifying question: do they want all mandates regardless of status? They said "all pending and active mandates". That implies both statuses. So we need to call user_mandates twice per user with status=active and status=pending. Then combine results. Let's do that. We'll call user_mandates({"name":"Parath","status":"active"}) and {"name":"Parath","status":"pending"} etc. Then combine. We'll produce combined list.
